# The menu bar helper, generated from menubar.yaml

For whoever next changes what the brainhouse menu bar shows. It answers: where
did `menubar/main.swift` go, and why is there still Swift in the repo.

**Built.** The helper is generated by [perch](https://michaelbaker.tech/perch/)
from `menubar.yaml`; only banner delivery is still hand-written.

## What moved

`menubar/main.swift` is gone. In its place:

```
menubar.yaml           the status item and the menu
menubar/Generated/     emitted by perch; committed, replaced whole on every build
menubar/Sources/       hand-written Swift; perch never reads or writes it
```

`npm run menubar:install` now shells to `perch install`, which compiles,
bundles, writes the LaunchAgent and bootstraps it. The 80 lines of bash that
did that by hand are gone; the label is unchanged (`com.brainhouse.menubar`),
so an existing install is replaced rather than duplicated.

## What the YAML says that the Swift could not

The old helper read a refused connection as "the server is not running". That
conflated two different failures, and only one of them is fixable from the
menu. Four states now:

| State | Means |
|---|---|
| `uninstalled` | no LaunchAgent plist — `npm run service:install` |
| `stopped` | plist on disk, launchd does not hold the label |
| `wedged` | launchd holds it and the server is not answering |
| `up` | answering |

`wedged` is the one the old helper could not name. It gets Restart rather than
Start, because `agent: server.start` is `bootstrap`, which fails on a job
launchd already holds — `restart` is bootout, wait, bootstrap.

## What stayed Swift, and why

`menubar/Sources/Alerts.swift` delivers the banners. perch's schema refuses
notifications deliberately, and this is the case that shows why: a banner fires
on a *transition*, not on a condition holding. Everything in the YAML is a pure
function of the last poll, with nothing remembered between polls — so the cursor
that makes each alert fire exactly once, and the silent seeding that stops a
helper restart replaying the server's backlog, have nowhere to live.

It reaches the generated app through `Controller`, which declares
`NSApplicationDelegate` and implements none of its lifecycle methods, so an
extension supplies the witness and AppKit calls it. perch reserves
`applicationWillFinishLaunching`, `applicationDidFinishLaunching` and
`applicationWillTerminate` for this, and has a test refusing to implement one —
doing so would shadow ours with no error and no warning.

A Swift extension takes no stored properties, so the hook is one line and the
cursor lives in an `AlertDelivery` singleton beside it.

The helper stays a dumb delivery arm: it posts whatever the feed hands it.
Muting is decided at enqueue time in `alertQueue.ts`, so filtering on `enabled`
here would only strand the cursor behind a backlog that then replays on unmute.

## Signing is load-bearing here

`app.sign: perch local signing` names an identity in this Mac's login keychain.
Without it the bundle is signed ad-hoc, the cdhash moves on every build, and
`UNUserNotificationCenter`'s authorization grant goes with it — so banners stop
until the prompt is answered again. That identity does not exist on anyone
else's machine; a clone would need its own, or the line removed.

`perch run` cannot test banners. It builds into a fresh temp directory on every
invocation, so the bundle is a new code identity each time and holds no
authorization grant — the helper logs `notifications not authorized` and the
status item works normally. Only `npm run menubar:install` exercises delivery.

## What the port gave up

**The "Notifications blocked in System Settings" line.** Only `Alerts.swift`
knows the authorization grant, and the generated menu is rebuilt from the last
poll every time it opens, so a hand-written item would be overwritten. Denial is
logged instead — `log show --predicate 'process == "brainhouse"'`.

**The `PORT` override.** The old install script baked `PORT` into the plist.
`8765` is now written in `menubar.yaml` and again in `Alerts.swift`; a different
port means editing both.

**The embedded WebKit dashboard.** Already unreachable — `useWebKitDashboard`
was `false` — so this deleted about 90 lines of dead window, key-monitor and
navigation-delegate code rather than a feature. Open Dashboard opens Chrome by
bundle id, falling back to the default browser, which is what it already did.

**The checkmark on the notifications toggle.** The schema has no checkmark, so
it is two `when:`-guarded items — Mute when enabled, Unmute when not.
